payload.body_md:
**This guide is the operating handbook for JVTO's private tours to Mount Bromo, Kawah Ijen and Tumpak Sewu.** It states what is required before you travel: the Ijen health screening mandated by BBKSDA regulation SE.1658/KSA.9/2024, the monthly Rijik closure that shuts the crater to every visitor, the 20% deposit and the balance deadlines, and what each route demands physically. PT Java Volcano Rendezvous has operated from Bondowoso, East Java since 2015 under NIB and TDUP 1102230032918.

Each topic below is summarised in one line and linked to the page that carries the full rules. Your Official E-Voucher / Invoice remains the binding document for your booking — this guide explains how things work, it does not override what your booking documents say.

---

## Operating status.

JVTO runs private, pre-booked tours on standard East Java routes. Access depends on weather, volcanic activity and park regulations, and we plan and adjust against official information from MAGMA Indonesia / PVMBG and local park management.

Partial restrictions are normal even while tours run: a single viewpoint, a hiking section or one waterfall path may close while the rest of the program continues. When a change is required, the options that apply are the ones written in your booking documents, not a separate discretionary policy.

Check your own government's travel advisory as well. This page is an operations update for JVTO routes, not a country-level advisory.

---

## Before you book.

**Booking, payment and Package Credit.** A 20% deposit confirms a booking; within 14 days of departure up to 100% may be due at the time of booking. Balance is due 5 days before Day 1 for card and QRIS, 3 days for bank transfer and Wise.
→ [Booking, payment and cancellation rules](/travel-guide/booking-information)

**Traffic police escort for groups.** For convoys of roughly 18 guests or more, JVTO can request an official Ditlantas escort for specific road segments. Approval is never guaranteed, and if escort is not written in your E-Voucher, the tour runs without it.
→ [How official police escort works](/travel-guide/police-escort-for-groups)

**ISIC student packages.** JVTO is a registered ISIC provider, ID 259268, with student-rate structures on selected tours for verified students.
→ [ISIC student packages](/isic/student-package)

---

## Health and safety.

**Ijen health screening.** Kawah Ijen is a night ascent to a crater rim at 2,386 m with sulfur gas exposure. Screening is required under BBKSDA regulation SE.1658/KSA.9/2024 and is included for eligible JVTO guests, performed by Dr. Ahmad Irwandanu (STR QN00001073380217) and recorded on a BSrE-signed digital certificate. Clearance reduces risk; it does not remove it, and a hike may still be modified or cancelled.
→ [What the Ijen health screening involves](/travel-guide/ijen-health-screening)

**Safety on tours.** Every JVTO tour is private — no mixed groups and no transport-only tickets — run by an 11-person permanent crew rather than freelancers, under a company led by an active Tourist Police officer.
→ [Safety procedures on JVTO tours](/travel-guide/safety-on-tours)

---

## Conditions and access.

**Weather, volcano alerts and closures.** Heavy rain, landslides, ash, gas, floods, road damage and official ceremonies all change access. JVTO distinguishes a partial closure from a full one and proposes alternatives where the route allows.
→ [How JVTO handles weather and closures](/travel-guide/weather-and-closures)

**The Rijik monthly closure.** Kawah Ijen closes to all visitors on the first Friday of every month, and has since March 2019, while volunteers clear an estimated 100–150 kg of waste from the crater. JVTO checks this calendar before confirming any Ijen itinerary.
→ [Rijik: the monthly closure day](/travel-guide/rijik-monthly-closure)

**When to travel.** Season changes what each route costs you in comfort and in the odds of seeing anything.
→ [Best time to visit East Java](/travel-guide/best-time-to-visit)

---

## Preparing to travel.

**Packing and fitness.** These routes are non-technical but physically demanding: early starts, night hiking, cold wind, steep paths and wet sections. The guide gives a self-check and a packing list; it is preparation, not medical approval.
→ [Packing list and fitness self-check](/travel-guide/packing-and-fitness)

**Mount Bromo logistics.** Departure times, jeep transfers and the sunrise viewpoint sequence.
→ [Mount Bromo logistics](/travel-guide/mount-bromo-logistics)

**Tumpak Sewu logistics.** Descent conditions, footing after rain and the viewpoint-versus-base decision.
→ [Tumpak Sewu logistics](/travel-guide/tumpak-sewu-logistics)

---

## If two documents disagree.

Where website wording differs from your booking documents, this is the order of priority:

1. Official E-Voucher / Invoice — specific to your booking
2. Booking, Payment & Cancellation Policy
3. Inclusions & Exclusions Policy
4. General website text and informal communication

The rule that settles most questions: **if it is not on the E-Voucher, it is not included.** Contact JVTO through the official channels listed on this site before travel if you are unsure how a rule applies to your booking.

---

## Common questions.

→ [Travel guide FAQ](/travel-guide/faq)

items.question: What is the Travel Guide for?
items.answer: This is JVTO's planning hub for safety rules, Ijen screening, closures/weather logic, packing/fitness, booking flow, and group escort context. It helps you prepare before departure.

items.question: What is the binding reference if anything differs?
items.answer: Your Official E-Voucher / Invoice (PDF) is the highest authority for your specific booking. If anything differs, follow the document precedence stated on this page and in the policy pack.

items.question: Which pages should I read before paying?
items.answer: Read /travel-guide/booking-information, then /policy/booking-payment-cancellation and /policy/inclusions-exclusions. Use /travel-guide/weather-and-closures for route uncertainty.

items.question: Where can I find the Ijen screening process?
items.answer: Read /travel-guide/ijen-health-screening. Screening is part of Ijen night hike logistics when applicable and may be required by local rules.

items.question: What should I do close to departure?
items.answer: Re-check /travel-guide/packing-and-fitness and /travel-guide/weather-and-closures. If you are unsure how a rule applies, verify via official channels before travel.
